keys.summary: The keys of the map, as a list.

values.summary: The values of the map, as a list.

pairs.summary: The map as a list of `[key, value]` pairs.
pairs.returns: `list` — one two element list per entry.
examples:
// sorting a map by value
list.sort_key(map.pairs(scores), -_:1);

get.summary: The value stored under a key, `null` when it is not there - the same thing the `:` operator does.
examples: m:'a';                 // the same thing, without importing

has.summary: Whether the key is in the map.
examples:
// it tells apart an absent key from one holding null
map.has(m, 'k');   // false, while m:'k' is null in both cases

put.summary: Writes a value under a key, replacing what was there.
put.returns: the previous value, `null` when the key was not there.
put.note: It changes the map in place. It is atomic even between tasks; a *sequence* of operations is not — for that there is `synchronize` in `core.task`.

delete.summary: Removes a key from the map.
delete.returns: the removed value, `null` when the key was not there.

length.summary: How many entries the map has.
